mechanism: Sertraline increases serotonin levels while lisdexamfetamine (a prodrug of amphetamine) increases catecholamine release; combined use elevates risk of serotonin syndrome and cardiovascular stimulation, though this combination is sometimes clinically used with careful monitoring.
action: Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, tremor, hyperthermia, rigidity) and cardiovascular effects; use together only when benefits justify risks, maintaining baseline vital signs and dose optimization.
